key_insight: MAS-PINN uses shared temporal features and network structure to learn multi-agent dynamics with lower computational and memory costs.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports scalable trajectory reconstruction and physical-parameter identification in coupled systems with partially observed states.
method: Represent agent trajectories using shared temporal features and agent-specific coefficients.
Alternate feature learning, coupled-trajectory fitting, and physical-parameter estimation.
Exploit local interactions with matrix-free coefficient updates instead of large global matrices.
evidence_signal: Experiments on Lorenz rings, Lotka–Volterra networks, and Rössler oscillators report improved trajectory and parameter accuracy over baselines, including partial-observation and unknown-topology settings, with substantial savings in coefficient fitting.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative speedups or error metrics, leaving practical gains for a target network to be verified.
paper_title: Efficient Modeling of Multi-Agent Systems via Structure-Aware Physics-Informed Learning
